recentItems.title: In Conversation: Josh Groban & Warner Music Group CEO Robert Kyncl
recentItems.description:
Josh Groban sits down with Warner Music Group CEO Robert Kyncl for an in-depth conversation about his album Cinematic and his journey as an artist who's been part of the WMG family for over 25 years. Reflecting on his journey as an artist, Josh shares insights into the experiences that have shaped his career, the creative process behind his music, and the importance of connecting with audiences through song.
Together, Josh and Robert explore the intersection of artistry and the business of music, discussing how the industry continues to evolve and what it takes to build a lasting career. From creativity and collaboration to the future of music, the conversation offers a unique perspective on the relationship between artists, their work, and the industry that brings it to the world.

recentItems.title: From Studio To Stage: The Makings of 'The Notebook' On Broadway
recentItems.description: Take a walk from our NYC offices to The Notebook's Broadway show, with Lead Producer Kurt Deutsch. A respected figure in the theatre community (Founder of Sh-K-Boom, Ghostlight Records), Kurt is also SVP, Warner Music Entertainment & Theatrical Ventures -- a unique role that sees him partner with a dynamic, diverse range of artists, composers and performers to elevate WMG talent in the musical theatre space.

recentItems.title: DIASPORA DIALOGUES
recentItems.description: People of African descent share dynamic connections across music, art, culture that transcend borders. We also share a common struggle against systemic racism given the global legacy of slavery and colonialism. This panel will highlight the SJF’s international partners, working across to address racial inequity within a global context, while accounting for the nuances of their home countries. During this event, SJF grantees from the UK, US, Colombia, Brazil, and Nigeria will discuss key racial justice issues and movement-building strategies in their countries.

recentItems.title: The WMG/BFF Social Justice Fund: Our Vision & Strategy
recentItems.description: This session will focus on the Fund’s grantmaking vision and social impact. With over $23M in grant commitments to date, the WMG/BFF SJF has supported a roster of more than 30 extraordinary organizations that power social change through education, criminal justice reform, and arts and culture.

recentItems.title: LEVERAGING CULTURE TO FUEL CRIMINAL JUSTICE REFORM
recentItems.description: The U.S. criminal justice system serves as a central form of racial control in the twenty-first century. Police brutality, racial profiling, school pushout, and sentencing discrepancies disproportionately affect people of color, with deadly consequences. These panelists have each invoked storytelling, media, and film to build a broader audience for their work, amplify voices of people in the carceral system, and shift public policy. How can social justice organizations best leverage media and entertainment to amplify their message, shift consciousness and attract unlikely allies? Where is the movement headed as creative partnerships like these deepen?
